description: Every table in the public schema is served over HTTP the moment it exists. Row-level security is not a feature to switch on later; without it, the table is published. These gates read the catalogue rather than the intent, because a policy that was written and a policy that is enforced look identical in a migration.

gates.title: Row-Level Security Is On For Every Table
gates.rule: Every table in the public schema has RLS enabled. The API serves the schema as it finds it, so a table without RLS is readable by anyone holding the publishable key, which ships in the page.
gates.fix: alter table public.<name> enable row level security, in a migration, plus the policies that restore the access the app needs.

gates.title: Every Protected Table Has A Policy
gates.rule: A table with RLS on and no policy denies everyone, which usually means a feature is silently broken rather than secure. Each table has at least one policy, or is recorded as deliberately closed.
gates.fix: Write the policy, or table-clear the table naming why it is closed to everyone.

gates.title: No Blanket Policy Stands In For A Real One
gates.rule: No policy uses a bare true for all roles on a table holding real data. A policy of true is RLS switched on in name only, and it reads as protection in every audit that counts policies rather than reading them.
gates.fix: Replace the blanket policy with one that names the role and the condition.

gates.title: The Anonymous Role Reaches Only What It Should
gates.rule: Tables granted to anon are the ones a signed-out visitor is meant to read. Anything else is reachable with the key in the page, whatever the application does with it.
gates.fix: revoke all on public.<name> from anon, in a migration.

gates.title: The Service Key Is Not In Anything The Browser Loads
gates.rule: No service-role key appears in source, in a build output, or in a variable with a client-side prefix. It bypasses every policy above, so one occurrence undoes the whole group.
gates.fix: Move the key to a server-side variable and rotate it, since a key that reached a bundle is public from then on.
